```{r}
    id,
    join_time,
    name = "n"
  ) %>%

  filter(
    n > 1
  )


cat(
  "\nResident duplicate keys:",
  nrow(resident_dup),
  "\n"
)


if (nrow(resident_dup) > 0) {
  stop("Duplicate corrected resident AKDE keys.")
}


# =============================================================================
# BUILD MIGRATORY LOOKUP
# =============================================================================

migratory_lookup <- final %>%

  transmute(

    id_phase =
      as.character(
        id_phase
      ),

    join_time =
      parse_time_safe(
        window_start
      ),

    new_akde_low =
      low,

    new_akde_est =
      est,

    new_akde_high =
      high
  )


migratory_dup <- migratory_lookup %>%

  count(
    id_phase,
    join_time,
    name = "n"
  ) %>%

  filter(
    n > 1
  )


cat(
  "Migratory duplicate keys:",
  nrow(migratory_dup),
  "\n"
)


if (nrow(migratory_dup) > 0) {
  stop("Duplicate corrected migratory AKDE keys.")
}


# =============================================================================
# PATCH FUNCTION
# =============================================================================

patch_akde_correctly <- function(
  input_file,
  output_file,
  dataset_name
) {

  cat(
    "\n",
    paste(rep("=", 100), collapse = ""),
    "\n",
    dataset_name,
    "\n",
    paste(rep("=", 100), collapse = ""),
    "\n",
    sep = ""
  )


  # ===========================================================================
  # READ ORIGINAL MODEL DATASET
  # ===========================================================================

  before <- read_csv(
    input_file,
    show_col_types = FALSE
  )


  original_names <- names(before)

  original_n <- nrow(before)


  cat(
    "\nRows:",
    original_n,
    "\n"
  )


  # ===========================================================================
  # CHECK REQUIRED ORIGINAL COLUMNS
  # ===========================================================================

  required <- c(
    "id",
    "date_time",
    "dataset",
    "akde_low",
    "akde_est",
    "akde_high"
  )


  missing_required <- setdiff(
    required,
    names(before)
  )


  if (length(missing_required) > 0) {

    stop(
      paste0(
        "Missing required columns: ",
        paste(
          missing_required,
          collapse = ", "
        )
      )
    )
  }


  # ===========================================================================
  # SEE ORIGINAL DATASET LABELS
  # ===========================================================================

  cat(
    "\nOriginal dataset label<LOCAL_PATH>"
  )


  print(
    before %>%
      count(
        dataset,
        name = "n"
      ),
    n = Inf
  )


  # ===========================================================================
  # PREPARE
  # ===========================================================================

  x <- before %>%

    mutate(

      .row_id =
        row_number(),

      id =
        as.character(
          id
        ),

      join_time =
        parse_time_safe(
          date_time
        ),

      dataset_clean =
        str_to_lower(
          str_trim(
            as.character(
              dataset
            )
          )
        ),

      had_old_akde =
        !is.na(akde_low) |
        !is.na(akde_est) |
        !is.na(akde_high)
    )


  # ===========================================================================
  # CHECK DATASET LABELS
  # ===========================================================================

  unknown_dataset <- x %>%

    filter(
      !dataset_clean %in%
        c(
          "resident",
          "migratory"
        )
    )


  if (nrow(unknown_dataset) > 0) {

    cat(
      "\nUnexpected dataset value<LOCAL_PATH>"
    )

    print(
      unique(
        unknown_dataset$dataset
      )
    )

    stop(
      "Unexpected dataset labels found."
    )
  }


  # ===========================================================================
  # IMPORTANT:
  # USE ORIGINAL id_phase IF IT ALREADY EXISTS
  # ===========================================================================

  if ("id_phase" %in% names(x)) {

    cat(
      "\nUsing existing id_phase column from original modeling dataset.\n"
    )


    x <- x %>%

      mutate(
        id_phase =
          as.character(
            id_phase
          )
      )

  } else {

    cat(
      "\nid_phase not found. Reconstructing it from phases.\n"
    )


    if (!"phases" %in% names(x)) {
      stop(
        "Migratory rows require either id_phase or phases."
      )
    }


    x <- x %>%

      mutate(

        phases_clean =
          phases %>%
          as.character() %>%
          str_trim() %>%
          str_squish() %>%
          str_replace_all(
            "_",
            " "
          ) %>%
          str_to_lower(),

        phase_num =
          str_extract(
            phases_clean,
            "\\d+"
          ),

        phase_label =
          case_when(

            !is.na(phase_num) ~
              paste0(
                "Phase_",
                phase_num
              ),

            TRUE ~
              phases_clean %>%
              str_to_title() %>%
              str_replace_all(
                "\\s+",
                "_"
              )
          ),

        id_phase =
          paste(
            id,
            phase_label,
            sep = "_"
          )
      )
  }


  # ===========================================================================
  # SPLIT BEFORE JOINING
  #
  # This reproduces the original AKDE workflow.
  # ===========================================================================

  resident_rows <- x %>%

    filter(
      dataset_clean == "resident"
    )


  migratory_rows <- x %>%

    filter(
      dataset_clean == "migratory"
    )


  cat(
    "\nResident rows:",
    nrow(resident_rows),
    "\n"
  )


  cat(
    "Migratory rows:",
    nrow(migratory_rows),
    "\n"
  )


  # ===========================================================================
  # RESIDENT JOIN
  # ===========================================================================

  resident_rows <- resident_rows %>%

    left_join(

      resident_lookup,

      by = c(
        "id",
        "join_time"
      )
    )


  # ===========================================================================
  # MIGRATORY JOIN
  # ===========================================================================

  migratory_rows <- migratory_rows %>%

    left_join(

      migratory_lookup,

      by = c(
        "id_phase",
        "join_time"
      )
    )


  # ===========================================================================
  # RECOMBINE
  # ===========================================================================

  x <- bind_rows(
    resident_rows,
    migratory_rows
  ) %>%

    arrange(
      .row_id
    )


  # ===========================================================================
  # MATCH DIAGNOSTICS
  # ===========================================================================

  match_summary <- x %>%

    mutate(

      corrected_match =
        !is.na(new_akde_low) &
        !is.na(new_akde_est) &
        !is.na(new_akde_high)

    ) %>%

    group_by(
      dataset
    ) %>%

    summarise(

      rows =
        n(),

      old_akde_rows =
        sum(
          had_old_akde
        ),

      corrected_matches =
        sum(
          corrected_match
        ),

      old_akde_without_corrected_match =
        sum(
          had_old_akde &
          !corrected_match
        ),

      .groups = "drop"
    )


  cat(
    "\nCorrected AKDE match summar<LOCAL_PATH>"
  )


  print(
    match_summary,
    n = Inf
  )


  # ===========================================================================
  # ROWS WHICH SHOULD MATCH BUT DO NOT
  # ===========================================================================

  missing_corrected <- x %>%

    filter(
      had_old_akde,
      (
        is.na(new_akde_low) |
        is.na(new_akde_est) |
        is.na(new_akde_high)
      )
    )


  cat(
    "\nRows that originally had AKDE:",
    sum(x$had_old_akde),
    "\n"
  )


  cat(
    "Rows missing corrected AKDE:",
    nrow(missing_corrected),
    "\n"
  )


  # ===========================================================================
  # IF THERE ARE STILL MISSES, STOP AND GIVE USEFUL DIAGNOSTICS
  # ===========================================================================

  if (nrow(missing_corrected) > 0) {

    diagnostic_file <- file.path(
      AE_BASE,
      paste0(
        dataset_name,
        "_MISSING_CORRECTED_AKDE_V2.csv"
      )
    )


    write_csv(
      missing_corrected,
      diagnostic_file
    )


    cat(
      "\nMissing rows by datase<LOCAL_PATH>"
    )


    print(
      missing_corrected %>%
        count(
          dataset,
          name = "missing"
        ),
      n = Inf
    )


    cat(
      "\nLargest missing group<LOCAL_PATH>"
    )


    if ("id_phase" %in% names(missing_corrected)) {

      print(
        missing_corrected %>%
          count(
            dataset,
            id,
            id_phase,
            name = "missing"
          ) %>%
          arrange(
            desc(missing)
          ) %>%
          slice_head(
            n = 30
          ),
        n = Inf
      )

    } else {

      print(
        missing_corrected %>%
          count(
            dataset,
            id,
            name = "missing"
          ) %>%
          arrange(
            desc(missing)
          ) %>%
          slice_head(
            n = 30
          ),
        n = Inf
      )
    }


    cat(
      "\nDiagnostic save<LOCAL_PATH>",
      diagnostic_file,
      "\n",
      sep = ""
    )


    stop(
      "Some original AKDE rows still lack corrected matches. Do not save yet."
    )
  }


  # ===========================================================================
  # REPLACE AKDE ONLY WHERE ORIGINAL AKDE EXISTED
  #
  # This preserves the original missingness pattern.
  # ===========================================================================

  x <- x %>%

    mutate(

      akde_low =
        if_else(
          had_old_akde,
          new_akde_low,
          NA_real_
        ),

      akde_est =
        if_else(
          had_old_akde,
          new_akde_est,
          NA_real_
        ),

      akde_high =
        if_else(
          had_old_akde,
          new_akde_high,
          NA_real_
        )
    )


  # ===========================================================================
  # RESTORE ORIGINAL DATASET STRUCTURE
  # ===========================================================================

  x_final <- x %>%

    arrange(
      .row_id
    ) %>%

    select(
      all_of(
        original_names
      )
    )


  # ===========================================================================
  # VERIFY ROW COUNT
  # ===========================================================================

  if (nrow(x_final) != original_n) {

    stop(
      "Row count changed."
    )
  }


  # ===========================================================================
  # VERIFY EVERY NON-AKDE COLUMN IS EXACTLY IDENTICAL
  # ===========================================================================

  non_akde_cols <- setdiff(
    original_names,
    c(
      "akde_low",
      "akde_est",
      "akde_high"
    )
  )


  identical_non_akde <- identical(
    before[
      non_akde_cols
    ],
    x_final[
      non_akde_cols
    ]
  )


  cat(
    "\nAll non-AKDE columns identical:",
    identical_non_akde,
    "\n"
  )


  if (!identical_non_akde) {

    stop(
      "A non-AKDE column changed. File not saved."
    )
  }


  # ===========================================================================
  # FINAL AKDE VALIDITY
  # ===========================================================================

  invalid <- x_final %>%

    filter(
      !is.na(akde_est),
      (
        akde_low <= 0 |
        akde_est <= 0 |
        akde_high <= 0 |
        akde_low > akde_est |
        akde_est > akde_high
      )
    )


  cat(
    "Invalid corrected AKDE rows:",
    nrow(invalid),
    "\n"
  )


  if (nrow(invalid) > 0) {

    stop(
      "Corrected AKDE validity check failed."
    )
  }


  # ===========================================================================
  # SHOW HOW MANY NUMBERS CHANGED
  # ===========================================================================

  change_summary <- tibble(

    variable = c(
      "akde_low",
      "akde_est",
      "akde_high"
    ),

    changed = c(

      sum(
        !is.na(before$akde_low) &
        before$akde_low !=
          x_final$akde_low
      ),

      sum(
        !is.na(before$akde_est) &
        before$akde_est !=
          x_final$akde_est
      ),

      sum(
        !is.na(before$akde_high) &
        before$akde_high !=
          x_final$akde_high
      )
    )
  )


  cat(
    "\nChanged AKDE value<LOCAL_PATH>"
  )


  print(
    change_summary
  )


  # ===========================================================================
  # UNIT-RATIO CHECK
  # ===========================================================================

  ratio <- before$akde_est /
    x_final$akde_est


  ratio <- ratio[
    is.finite(ratio) &
    ratio > 0
  ]


  cat(
    "\nOld / corrected akde_est rati<LOCAL_PATH>"
  )


  print(
    summary(
      ratio
    )
  )


  # ===========================================================================
  # SAVE
  # ===========================================================================

  write_csv(
    x_final,
    output_file
  )


  cat(
    "\n",
    paste(rep("=", 100), collapse = ""),
    "\n",
    "SUCCESS\n",
    paste(rep("=", 100), collapse = ""),
    "\n",
    sep = ""
  )


  cat(
    "\nSave<LOCAL_PATH>",
    output_file,
    "\n",
    sep = ""
  )


  return(
    x_final
  )
}


# =============================================================================
# RUN CWD- TRAINING FIRST
#
# Let's verify this one before touching the CWD+ file.
# =============================================================================

train_fixed <- patch_akde_correctly(

  input_file =
    TRAIN_FILE,

  output_file =
    TRAIN_OUT,

  dataset_name =
    "CWD_negative_training"
)
```

## Double check the measurement of AKDE
```{r}
# =============================================================================
# PRE-MERGE AKDE UNIT AUDIT
#
# Purpose:
# Prove that BOTH resident and migratory corrected AKDE tables are in the
# exact same measurement unit BEFORE joining into training/testing data.
#
# Required result:
#
#   akde_unit = "square_kilometers"
#
# for EVERY corrected AKDE row.
# =============================================================================

library(dplyr)
library(tibble)
library(readr)
library(stringr)


# =============================================================================
# 1. MAKE SURE BOTH OBJECTS EXIST
# =============================================================================

if (!exists("resident_corrected")) {
  stop("resident_corrected is missing from the workspace.")
}

if (!exists("final")) {
  stop("final migratory corrected AKDE object is missing from the workspace.")
}


# =============================================================================
# 2. LABEL THE TWO SOURCES
# =============================================================================

resident_audit <- resident_corrected %>%
  mutate(
    movement_source = "Resident"
  )


migratory_audit <- final %>%
  mutate(
    movement_source = "Migratory"
  )


# =============================================================================
# 3. UNIT LABEL SUMMARY — RESIDENT
# =============================================================================

cat(
  "\n",
  paste(rep("=", 100), collapse = ""),
  "\n",
  "RESIDENT UNIT SUMMARY\n",
  paste(rep("=", 100), collapse = ""),
  "\n",
  sep = ""
)


resident_unit_summary <- resident_audit %>%
  count(
    akde_unit,
    source_unit,
    name = "n"
  )


print(
  resident_unit_summary,
  n = Inf
)


# =============================================================================
# 4. UNIT LABEL SUMMARY — MIGRATORY
# =============================================================================

cat(
  "\n",
  paste(rep("=", 100), collapse = ""),
  "\n",
  "MIGRATORY UNIT SUMMARY\n",
  paste(rep("=", 100), collapse = ""),
  "\n",
  sep = ""
)


migratory_unit_summary <- migratory_audit %>%
  count(
    akde_unit,
    source_unit,
    name = "n"
  )


print(
  migratory_unit_summary,
  n = Inf
)


# =============================================================================
# 5. HARD CHECK:
# EVERY ROW MUST SAY square_kilometers
# =============================================================================

resident_bad_unit <- resident_audit %>%
  filter(
    is.na(akde_unit) |
    akde_unit != "square_kilometers"
  )


migratory_bad_unit <- migratory_audit %>%
  filter(
    is.na(akde_unit) |
    akde_unit != "square_kilometers"
  )


cat(
  "\nResident rows NOT labeled square_kilometers:",
  nrow(resident_bad_unit),
  "\n"
)


cat(
  "Migratory rows NOT labeled square_kilometers:",
  nrow(migratory_bad_unit),
  "\n"
)


# =============================================================================
# 6. CHECK ORIGINAL EXTRACTION UNIT
#
# For the corrected rows extracted using:
#
#     summary(UD, units = FALSE)
#
# source_unit should indicate square meters.
#
# Those values were then divided by 1e6 to produce km².
# =============================================================================

resident_source_check <- resident_audit %>%
  mutate(
    source_is_square_meters =
      str_detect(
        str_to_lower(
          as.character(source_unit)
        ),
        "square meter"
      )
  ) %>%
  count(
    source_is_square_meters,
    name = "n"
  )


migratory_source_check <- migratory_audit %>%
  mutate(
    source_is_square_meters =
      str_detect(
        str_to_lower(
          as.character(source_unit)
        ),
        "square meter"
      )
  ) %>%
  count(
    source_is_square_meters,
    name = "n"
  )


cat(
  "\nResident source-unit chec<LOCAL_PATH>"
)

print(
  resident_source_check,
  n = Inf
)


cat(
  "\nMigratory source-unit chec<LOCAL_PATH>"
)

print(
  migratory_source_check,
  n = Inf
)


# =============================================================================
# 7. NUMERIC VALIDITY
# =============================================================================

check_numeric <- function(df) {

  df %>%
    summarise(

      rows =
        n(),

      missing_low =
        sum(
          is.na(low)
        ),

      missing_est =
        sum(
          is.na(est)
        ),

      missing_high =
        sum(
          is.na(high)
        ),

      nonfinite_low =
        sum(
          !is.na(low) &
          !is.finite(low)
        ),

      nonfinite_est =
        sum(
          !is.na(est) &
          !is.finite(est)
        ),

      nonfinite_high =
        sum(
          !is.na(high) &
          !is.finite(high)
        ),

      nonpositive_low =
        sum(
          !is.na(low) &
          low <= 0
        ),

      nonpositive_est =
        sum(
          !is.na(est) &
          est <= 0
        ),

      nonpositive_high =
        sum(
          !is.na(high) &
          high <= 0
        ),

      bad_ci_order =
        sum(
          !is.na(low) &
          !is.na(est) &
          !is.na(high) &
          (
            low > est |
            est > high
          )
        )
    )
}


cat(
  "\n",

  "\n",
  "RESIDENT NUMERIC VALIDATION\n",
  paste(rep("=", 100), collapse = ""),
  "\n",
  sep = ""
)


resident_numeric <- check_numeric(
  resident_audit
)

print(

)


cat(
  "\n",
  paste(rep("=", 100), collapse = ""),

  "MIGRATORY NUMERIC VALIDATION\n",

  "\n",

)


migratory_numeric <- check_numeric(
  migratory_audit
)

print(
  migratory_numeric,
  width = Inf
)


# =============================================================================
# 8. COMBINE JUST FOR UNIT AUDIT
#
# IMPORTANT:
# This is NOT the model merge.
#
# We're simply combining the corrected AKDE tables to prove they use
# the same measurement system.
# =============================================================================

all_corrected_akde <- bind_rows(

  resident_audit %>%
    select(
      movement_source,
      id,
      window_start,
      low,
      est,
      high,
      akde_unit,
      source_unit
    ),

  migratory_audit %>%
    select(
      movement_source,
      id,
      window_start,
      low,
      est,
      high,
      akde_unit,
      source_unit
    )
)


# =============================================================================
# 9. GLOBAL UNIT SUMMARY
# =============================================================================

cat(
  "\n",
  paste(rep("=", 100), collapse = ""),
  "\n",
  "COMBINED PRE-MERGE UNIT SUMMARY\n",
  paste(rep("=", 100), collapse = ""),
  "\n",
  sep = ""
)


combined_unit_summary <- all_corrected_akde %>%
  count(
    movement_source,
    akde_unit,
    name = "rows"
  )


print(
  combined_unit_summary,
  n = Inf
)


# =============================================================================
# 10. HOW MANY DISTINCT STANDARDIZED UNITS EXIST?
# =============================================================================

distinct_units <- all_corrected_akde %>%
  distinct(
    akde_unit
  )


cat(
  "\nNumber of distinct standardized AKDE units:",
  nrow(distinct_units),
  "\n"
)


print(
  distinct_units
)


# =============================================================================
# 11. SIDE-BY-SIDE MAGNITUDE SUMMARY
#
# This does NOT prove units, but it helps us identify obvious anomalies after
# confirming that the unit labels are consistent.
# =============================================================================

magnitude_summary <- all_corrected_akde %>%

  group_by(
    movement_source
  ) %>%

  summarise(

    n =
      n(),

    min =
      min(
        est,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    p001 =
      quantile(
        est,
        0.001,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    p01 =
      quantile(
        est,
        0.01,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    p05 =
      quantile(
        est,
        0.05,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    median =
      median(
        est,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    mean =
      mean(
        est,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    p95 =
      quantile(
        est,
        0.95,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    p99 =
      quantile(
        est,
        0.99,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    p999 =
      quantile(
        est,
        0.999,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    max =
      max(
        est,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    .groups = "drop"
  )


cat(
  "\n",
  paste(rep("=", 100), collapse = ""),
  "\n",
  "CORRECTED AKDE MAGNITUDE SUMMARY — km²\n",
  paste(rep("=", 100), collapse = ""),
  "\n",
  sep = ""
)


print(
  magnitude_summary,
  width = Inf
)


# =============================================================================
# 12. HARD PASS / FAIL
# =============================================================================

resident_pass <- (
  nrow(resident_bad_unit) == 0 &&
  resident_numeric$missing_low == 0 &&
  resident_numeric$missing_est == 0 &&
  resident_numeric$missing_high == 0 &&
  resident_numeric$nonfinite_low == 0 &&
  resident_numeric$nonfinite_est == 0 &&
  resident_numeric$nonfinite_high == 0 &&
  resident_numeric$nonpositive_low == 0 &&
  resident_numeric$nonpositive_est == 0 &&
  resident_numeric$nonpositive_high == 0 &&
  resident_numeric$bad_ci_order == 0
)


migratory_pass <- (
  nrow(migratory_bad_unit) == 0 &&
  migratory_numeric$missing_low == 0 &&
  migratory_numeric$missing_est == 0 &&
  migratory_numeric$missing_high == 0 &&
  migratory_numeric$nonfinite_low == 0 &&
  migratory_numeric$nonfinite_est == 0 &&
  migratory_numeric$nonfinite_high == 0 &&
  migratory_numeric$nonpositive_low == 0 &&
  migratory_numeric$nonpositive_est == 0 &&
  migratory_numeric$nonpositive_high == 0 &&
  migratory_numeric$bad_ci_order == 0
)


same_standardized_unit <- (
  nrow(distinct_units) == 1 &&
  distinct_units$akde_unit[1] ==
    "square_kilometers"
)


# =============================================================================
# 13. FINAL RESULT
# =============================================================================

cat(
  "\n",
  paste(rep("=", 100), collapse = ""),
  "\n",
  "PRE-MERGE UNIT AUDIT RESULT\n",
  paste(rep("=", 100), collapse = ""),
  "\n",
  sep = ""
)


cat(
  "\nResident passed:",
  resident_pass,
  "\n"
)

cat(
  "Migratory passed:",
  migratory_pass,
  "\n"
)

cat(
  "Single standardized unit:",
  same_standardized_unit,
  "\n"
)


if (
  resident_pass &&
  migratory_pass &&
  same_standardized_unit
) {

  cat(
    "\n",
    paste(rep("=", 100), collapse = ""),
    "\n",
    "PASS: ALL CORRECTED AKDE VALUES WERE IN SQUARE KILOMETERS BEFORE MODEL MERGE\n",
    paste(rep("=", 100), collapse = ""),
    "\n",
    sep = ""
  )

} else {

  stop(
    paste0(
      "PRE-MERGE UNIT AUDIT FAILED. ",
      "Do not continue with model data."
    )
  )
}
```

### Final EDA before training etc
```{r}
# =============================================================================
# FINAL AKDE EDA — CORRECTED TRAINING DATA
#
# Questions:
#
# 1. Does EVERY corrected AKDE value in the training CSV exactly correspond
#    to the corrected resident/migratory source table?
#
# 2. What is the corrected AKDE distribution in km²?
#
# 3. Are there unusually small or large corrected values?
#
# 4. Are AKDE confidence intervals sensible?
#
# 5. Are there abrupt adjacent-window jumps remaining after unit correction?
#
# IMPORTANT:
# Extreme values are FLAGGED for inspection, not automatically removed.
# =============================================================================


library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(stringr)
library(tibble)
library(ggplot2)


# =============================================================================
# 1. PATHS
# =============================================================================

AE_BASE <- "<LOCAL_PATH>"

TRAIN_FILE <- file.path(
  AE_BASE,
  "CWD_negative_training_with_seasons2_AKDE_FIXED.csv"
)

EDA_DIR <- file.path(
  AE_BASE,
  "AKDE_FINAL_EDA"
)

dir.create(
  EDA_DIR,
  recursive = TRUE,
  showWarnings = FALSE
)


# =============================================================================
# 2. REQUIRED CORRECTED SOURCE OBJECTS
# =============================================================================

if (!exists("resident_corrected")) {
  stop("resident_corrected is not in the R workspace.")
}

if (!exists("final")) {
  stop("final migratory corrected AKDE object is not in the R workspace.")
}


# =============================================================================
# 3. SAFE DATETIME PARSER
# =============================================================================

parse_time_safe <- function(x) {

  if (inherits(x, "POSIXt")) {
    return(
      as.POSIXct(
        x,
        tz = "UTC"
      )
    )
  }

  x <- trimws(
    as.character(x)
  )

  out <- as.POSIXct(
    x,
    format = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%OS",
    tz = "UTC"
  )

  bad <- is.na(out) & !is.na(x) & nzchar(x)

  if (any(bad)) {

    out2 <- as.POSIXct(
      x[bad],
      format = "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%OS",
      tz = "UTC"
    )

    out[bad] <- out2
  }

  bad <- is.na(out) & !is.na(x) & nzchar(x)

  if (any(bad)) {

    print(
      head(
        unique(
          x[bad]
        ),
        20
      )
    )

    stop(
      paste(
        sum(bad),
        "timestamps could not be parsed."
      )
    )
  }

  out
}


# =============================================================================
# 4. LOAD CORRECTED TRAINING DATA
# =============================================================================

train <- read_csv(
  TRAIN_FILE,
  show_col_types = FALSE
)


cat(
  "\n",
  paste(rep("=", 100), collapse = ""),
  "\n",
  "CORRECTED TRAINING DATA\n",
  paste(rep("=", 100), collapse = ""),
  "\n",
  sep = ""
)


cat(
  "\nRows:",
  nrow(train),
  "\n"
)

cat(
  "IDs:",
  n_distinct(train$id),
  "\n"
)


required <- c(
  "id",
  "dataset",
  "date_time",
  "akde_low",
  "akde_est",
  "akde_high"
)


missing_required <- setdiff(
  required,
  names(train)
)


if (length(missing_required) > 0) {

  stop(
    paste(
      "Missing:",
      paste(
        missing_required,
        collapse = ", "
      )
    )
  )
}


if (!"id_phase" %in% names(train)) {
  train$id_phase <- NA_character_
}


train <- train %>%

  mutate(

    .row_id =
      row_number(),

    id =
      as.character(
        id
      ),

    id_phase =
      as.character(
        id_phase
      ),

    dataset_clean =
      str_to_lower(
        str_trim(
          as.character(
            dataset
          )
        )
      ),

    join_time =
      parse_time_safe(
        date_time
      )
  )


# =============================================================================
# 5. BASIC MISSINGNESS
# =============================================================================

missing_summary <- train %>%

  group_by(
    dataset
  ) %>%

  summarise(

    rows =
      n(),

    rows_with_akde =
      sum(
        !is.na(akde_est)
      ),

    rows_without_akde =
      sum(
        is.na(akde_est)
      ),

    percent_with_akde =
      round(
        100 *
        rows_with_akde /
        rows,
        2
      ),

    .groups = "drop"
  )


cat(
  "\nAKDE coverag<LOCAL_PATH>"
)

print(
  missing_summary,
  n = Inf
)


# =============================================================================
# 6. BUILD SOURCE LOOKUPS
# =============================================================================

resident_source <- resident_corrected %>%

  transmute(

    id =
      as.character(
        id
      ),

    join_time =
      parse_time_safe(
        window_start
      ),

    source_low =
      low,

    source_est =
      est,

    source_high =
      high
  )


migratory_source <- final %>%

  transmute(

    id_phase =
      as.character(
        id_phase
      ),

    join_time =
      parse_time_safe(
        window_start
      ),

    source_low =
      low,

    source_est =
      est,

    source_high =
      high
  )


# =============================================================================
# 7. CHECK LOOKUP UNIQUENESS AGAIN
# =============================================================================

resident_duplicates <- resident_source %>%

  count(
    id,
    join_time
  ) %>%

  filter(
    n > 1
  )


migratory_duplicates <- migratory_source %>%

  count(
    id_phase,
    join_time
  ) %>%

  filter(
    n > 1
  )


cat(
  "\nResident source duplicate keys:",
  nrow(resident_duplicates),
  "\n"
)

cat(
  "Migratory source duplicate keys:",
  nrow(migratory_duplicates),
  "\n"
)


if (
  nrow(resident_duplicates) > 0 ||
  nrow(migratory_duplicates) > 0
) {

  stop(
    "Corrected source lookup contains duplicate keys."
  )
}


# =============================================================================
# 8. END-TO-END PROVENANCE CHECK
#
# This is the most important check.
#
# Does every value now in the modeling CSV actually equal the corrected
# source AKDE value?
# =============================================================================

resident_check <- train %>%

  filter(
    dataset_clean == "resident"
  ) %>%

  left_join(
    resident_source,
    by = c(
      "id",
      "join_time"
    )
  )


migratory_check <- train %>%

  filter(
    dataset_clean == "migratory"
  ) %>%

  left_join(
    migratory_source,
    by = c(
      "id_phase",
      "join_time"
    )
  )


provenance <- bind_rows(
  resident_check,
  migratory_check
) %>%

  arrange(
    .row_id
  )


# =============================================================================
# 9. NUMERIC EQUALITY FUNCTION
#
# Allows tiny floating-point differences from CSV writing/reading.
# =============================================================================

same_number <- function(x, y, tolerance = 1e-10) {

  !is.na(x) &
  !is.na(y) &
  abs(x - y) <=
    tolerance *
    pmax(
      1,
      abs(x),
      abs(y)
    )
}


provenance <- provenance %>%

  mutate(

    low_matches =
      case_when(

        is.na(akde_low) &
        is.na(source_low) ~
          TRUE,

        TRUE ~
          same_number(
            akde_low,
            source_low
          )
      ),

    est_matches =
      case_when(

        is.na(akde_est) &
        is.na(source_est) ~
          TRUE,

        TRUE ~
          same_number(
            akde_est,
            source_est
          )
      ),

    high_matches =
      case_when(

        is.na(akde_high) &
        is.na(source_high) ~
          TRUE,

        TRUE ~
          same_number(
            akde_high,
            source_high
          )
      )
  )


# =============================================================================
# IMPORTANT:
#
# Rows intentionally lacking AKDE in the modeling dataset were preserved
# as missing. For provenance, only require matches where model AKDE exists.
# =============================================================================

provenance_bad <- provenance %>%

  filter(
    !is.na(akde_est),
    (
      is.na(source_est) |
      !low_matches |
      !est_matches |
      !high_matches
    )
  )


cat(
  "\n",
  paste(rep("=", 100), collapse = ""),
  "\n",
  "END-TO-END AKDE PROVENANCE CHECK\n",
  paste(rep("=", 100), collapse = ""),
  "\n",
  sep = ""
)


cat(
  "\nRows with AKDE in model data:",
  sum(
    !is.na(
      provenance$akde_est
    )
  ),
  "\n"
)


cat(
  "Rows NOT matching corrected source:",
  nrow(provenance_bad),
  "\n"
)


if (nrow(provenance_bad) > 0) {

  write_csv(
    provenance_bad,
    file.path(
      EDA_DIR,
      "PROVENANCE_MISMATCHES.csv"
    )
  )

  stop(
    "Corrected model AKDE does not perfectly match the source tables."
  )
}


cat(
  "\nPASS: every non-missing model AKDE value matches its corrected source.\n"
)


# =============================================================================
# 10. IMPOSSIBLE / INVALID VALUES
# =============================================================================

invalid <- train %>%

  filter(
    !is.na(akde_est),
    (
      !is.finite(akde_low) |
      !is.finite(akde_est) |
      !is.finite(akde_high) |
      akde_low <= 0 |
      akde_est <= 0 |
      akde_high <= 0 |
      akde_low > akde_est |
      akde_est > akde_high
    )
  )


cat(
  "\nInvalid corrected AKDE rows:",
  nrow(invalid),
  "\n"
)


if (nrow(invalid) > 0) {

  write_csv(
    invalid,
    file.path(
      EDA_DIR,
      "INVALID_CORRECTED_AKDE.csv"
    )
  )

  stop(
    "Invalid corrected AKDE values found."
  )
}


# =============================================================================
# 11. DISTRIBUTION SUMMARY
#
# All values below are km².
# =============================================================================

distribution_summary <- train %>%

  filter(
    !is.na(akde_est)
  ) %>%

  group_by(
    dataset
  ) %>%

  summarise(

    n =
      n(),

    minimum =
      min(
        akde_est
      ),

    p001 =
      quantile(
        akde_est,
        0.001
      ),

    p01 =
      quantile(
        akde_est,
        0.01
      ),

    p05 =
      quantile(
        akde_est,
        0.05
      ),

    p25 =
      quantile(
        akde_est,
        0.25
      ),

    median =
      median(
        akde_est
      ),

    mean =
      mean(
        akde_est
      ),

    p75 =
      quantile(
        akde_est,
        0.75
      ),

    p95 =
      quantile(
        akde_est,
        0.95
      ),

    p99 =
      quantile(
        akde_est,
        0.99
      ),

    p999 =
      quantile(
        akde_est,
        0.999
      ),

    maximum =
      max(
        akde_est
      ),

    .groups = "drop"
  )


cat(
  "\n",
  paste(rep("=", 100), collapse = ""),
  "\n",
  "CORRECTED AKDE DISTRIBUTION — km²\n",
  paste(rep("=", 100), collapse = ""),
  "\n",
  sep = ""
)


print(

  width = Inf
)


write_csv(

    EDA_DIR,
    "01_corrected_distribution_summary.csv"
  )
)


# =============================================================================
# 12. CI WIDTH
#
# Relative CI width:
#
#     (high - low) / estimate
#
# This lets us find unstable or very uncertain windows.
# =============================================================================

train <- train %>%

  mutate(

    relative_ci_width =
      case_when(

        !is.na(akde_est) &
        akde_est > 0 ~
          (
            akde_high -
            akde_low
          ) /
          akde_est,

        TRUE ~
          NA_real_
      )
  )


ci_summary <- train %>%

  filter(
    !is.na(
      relative_ci_width
    )
  ) %>%

  group_by(
    dataset
  ) %>%

  summarise(

    median =
      median(
        relative_ci_width
      ),

    p90 =
      quantile(
        relative_ci_width,
        0.90
      ),

    p95 =
      quantile(
        relative_ci_width,
        0.95
      ),

    p99 =
      quantile(
        relative_ci_width,
        0.99
      ),

    p999 =
      quantile(
        relative_ci_width,
        0.999
      ),

    maximum =
      max(
        relative_ci_width
      ),

    .groups = "drop"
  )


cat(
  "\n",
  paste(rep("=", 100), collapse = ""),
  "\n",
  "RELATIVE AKDE CI WIDTH\n",
  paste(rep("=", 100), collapse = ""),
  "\n",
  sep = ""
)


print(
  ci_summary,
  width = Inf
)


# =============================================================================
# 13. ROBUST EXTREME-VALUE FLAG ON LOG10 SCALE
#
# This is only an inspection flag.
#
# It is NOT a reason to delete observations.
# =============================================================================

train <- train %>%

  mutate(

    log10_akde =
      if_else(
        !is.na(akde_est) &
        akde_est > 0,
        log10(
          akde_est
        ),
        NA_real_
      )
  ) %>%

  group_by(
    dataset
  ) %>%

  mutate(

    log_median =
      median(
        log10_akde,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    log_mad =
      mad(
        log10_akde,
        center =
          log_median,
        constant =
          1.4826,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    robust_distance =
      if_else(
        log_mad > 0,
        abs(
          log10_akde -
          log_median
        ) /
        log_mad,
        NA_real_
      ),

    extreme_flag =
      robust_distance > 6
  ) %>%

  ungroup()


extreme_summary <- train %>%

  group_by(
    dataset
  ) %>%

  summarise(

    akde_rows =
      sum(
        !is.na(akde_est)
      ),

    extreme_rows =
      sum(
        extreme_flag,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    extreme_percent =
      100 *
      extreme_rows /
      akde_rows,

    .groups = "drop"
  )


cat(
  "\n",
  paste(rep("=", 100), collapse = ""),
  "\n",
  "ROBUST EXTREME-VALUE FLAGS\n",
  paste(rep("=", 100), collapse = ""),
  "\n",
  sep = ""
)


print(
  extreme_summary,
  width = Inf
)


extreme_rows <- train %>%

  filter(
    extreme_flag
  ) %>%

  arrange(
    desc(
      robust_distance
    )
  ) %>%

  select(
    id,
    id_phase,
    dataset,
    date_time,
    akde_low,
    akde_est,
    akde_high,
    relative_ci_width,
    robust_distance
  )


write_csv(
  extreme_rows,
  file.path(
    EDA_DIR,
    "02_flagged_extreme_AKDE_rows.csv"
  )
)

id_summary <- train %>%

  group_by(

    mean =

      ),

      quantile(

        0.99
      ),

    maximum =
      max(
        akde_est
      ),

    median_relative_ci =
      median(
        relative_ci_width,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

  arrange(

    )

cat(
  "\n",

  )

# =============================================================================
# 15. TRAJECTORY GROUP
#
# Resident:
#     individual deer
#
# Migratory:
#     individual + phase
#
# We MUST keep migratory phases separate for adjacent-window comparisons.
# =============================================================================

train <- train %>%

  mutate(

    trajectory_group =
      case_when(

        dataset_clean ==
          "migratory" &
        !is.na(id_phase) ~
          id_phase,

        TRUE ~
          id
      )
  )


# =============================================================================
# 16. ADJACENT AKDE CHANGE ANALYSIS
#
# This is one of the strongest checks that the display-unit discontinuity
# has actually disappeared.
# =============================================================================

jump_analysis <- train %>%

  filter(
    !is.na(akde_est),
    akde_est > 0
  ) %>%

  arrange(
    trajectory_group,
    join_time
  ) %>%

  group_by(
    trajectory_group
  ) %>%

  mutate(

    previous_time =
      lag(
        join_time
      ),

    previous_akde =
      lag(
        akde_est
      ),

    time_difference_hours =
      as.numeric(
        difftime(
          join_time,
          previous_time,
          units = "hours"
        )
      ),

    raw_ratio =
      akde_est /
      previous_akde,

    fold_change =
      pmax(
        raw_ratio,
        1 /
        raw_ratio
      )
  ) %>%

  ungroup()


# =============================================================================
# 17. ADJACENT-JUMP SUMMARY
# =============================================================================

jump_summary <- jump_analysis %>%

  filter(
    is.finite(
      fold_change
    )
  ) %>%

  group_by(
    dataset
  ) %>%

  summarise(

    comparisons =
      n(),

    median =
      median(
        fold_change
      ),

    p90 =
      quantile(
        fold_change,
        0.90
      ),

    p95 =
      quantile(
        fold_change,
        0.95
      ),

    p99 =
      quantile(
        fold_change,
        0.99
      ),

    p999 =
      quantile(
        fold_change,
        0.999
      ),

    maximum =
      max(
        fold_change
      ),

    over_2x =
      sum(
        fold_change > 2
      ),

    over_5x =
      sum(
        fold_change > 5
      ),

    over_10x =
      sum(
        fold_change > 10
      ),

    over_100x =
      sum(
        fold_change > 100
      ),

    over_1000x =
      sum(
        fold_change > 1000
      ),

    over_1million_x =
      sum(
        fold_change > 1e6
      ),

    .groups = "drop"
  )


cat(
  "\n",
  paste(rep("=", 100), collapse = ""),
  "\n",
  "ADJACENT CORRECTED AKDE CHANGE SUMMARY\n",
  paste(rep("=", 100), collapse = ""),
  "\n",
  sep = ""
)


print(
  jump_summary,
  width = Inf
)


write_csv(
  jump_summary,
  file.path(
    EDA_DIR,
    "04_adjacent_AKDE_jump_summary.csv"
  )
)


# =============================================================================
# 18. LARGEST REMAINING ADJACENT JUMPS
# =============================================================================

largest_jumps <- jump_analysis %>%

  filter(
    is.finite(
      fold_change
    )
  ) %>%

  arrange(
    desc(
      fold_change
    )
  ) %>%

  select(
    dataset,
    id,
    id_phase,
    trajectory_group,

cat(
```

### Targted AKDE investigation
```{r}
# =============================================================================
# TARGETED AKDE QC FOR THE ONLY SUSPICIOUS CASES
#
# A50 Phase 2
# F91 Phase 3
# A55 Phase 2
# F97 Resident
#
# Nothing is filtered or changed.
# =============================================================================

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(readr)
library(tibble)


# =============================================================================
# 1. MIGRATORY SOURCE TABLE WITH FIX COUNTS
# =============================================================================

migratory_qc <- final %>%

  filter(
    id_phase %in% c(
      "A50_Phase_2",
      "F91_Phase_3",
      "A55_Phase_2"
    )
  ) %>%

  mutate(
    relative_ci_width =
      (high - low) / est
  ) %>%

  arrange(
    id_phase,
    window_start
  ) %>%

  group_by(
    id_phase
  ) %>%

  mutate(
    previous_est =
      lag(est),

    adjacent_ratio =
      est / previous_est,

    fold_change =
      pmax(
        adjacent_ratio,
        1 / adjacent_ratio
      )
  ) %>%

  ungroup()


# =============================================================================
# 2. SUMMARY BY MIGRATORY DEER / PHASE
# =============================================================================

migratory_qc_summary <- migratory_qc %>%

  group_by(
    id,
    id_phase
  ) %>%

  summarise(

    n_windows =
      n(),

    min_fixes =
      min(
        n_fixes_window,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    median_fixes =
      median(
        n_fixes_window,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    max_fixes =
      max(
        n_fixes_window,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    min_est =
      min(
        est,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    median_est =
      median(
        est,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    max_est =
      max(
        est,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    max_relative_ci =
      max(
        relative_ci_width,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    max_adjacent_fold_change =
      max(
        fold_change,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    .groups = "drop"
  )


cat(

  "SUSPICIOUS MIGRATORY PHASE SUMMARY\n",
```

### Large step investigation and unrealistic movements
```{r}
# =============================================================================
# PRIVACY-SAFE RAW GPS QC
#
# DOES NOT PRINT OR EXPORT:
#   latitude
#   longitude
#   absolute x
#   absolute y
#
# Uses coordinates internally only to calculate:
#   step distance
#   speed
#   relative track geometry
# =============================================================================

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(tibble)


# =============================================================================
# 1. PREPARE TARGET TELEMETRY
# =============================================================================

migr_raw_qc <- migr_clean %>%

  filter(
    id_phase %in% c(
      "A50_Phase_2",
      "F91_Phase_3",
      "A55_Phase_2"
    )
  ) %>%

  mutate(
    date_time =
      as.POSIXct(
        date_time,
        tz = "UTC"
      )
  ) %>%

  arrange(
    id_phase,
    date_time
  ) %>%

  group_by(
    id_phase
  ) %>%

  mutate(

    previous_time =
      lag(date_time),

    gap_hours =
      as.numeric(
        difftime(
          date_time,
          previous_time,
          units = "hours"
        )
      ),

    # ----------------------------------------------------------
    # Distance derived internally.
    # Absolute coordinates are never displayed.
    # ----------------------------------------------------------

    step_m =
      sqrt(
        (x - lag(x))^2 +
        (y - lag(y))^2
      ),

    step_km =
      step_m / 1000,

    speed_kmh =
      step_km /
      gap_hours,

    # ----------------------------------------------------------
    # Relative/de-identified coordinates.
    #
    # First fix becomes (0, 0).
    # These reveal movement shape but NOT absolute location.
    # ----------------------------------------------------------

    relative_x_km =
      (x - first(x)) / 1000,

    relative_y_km =
      (y - first(y)) / 1000
  ) %>%

  ungroup()


# =============================================================================
# 2. OVERALL RAW TELEMETRY SUMMARY
# =============================================================================

raw_summary <- migr_raw_qc %>%

  group_by(
    id,
    id_phase
  ) %>%

  summarise(

    n_fixes =
      n(),

    median_gap_hours =
      median(
        gap_hours,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    p95_gap_hours =
      quantile(
        gap_hours,
        0.95,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    max_gap_hours =
      max(
        gap_hours,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    median_step_km =
      median(
        step_km,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    p95_step_km =
      quantile(
        step_km,
        0.95,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    p99_step_km =
      quantile(
        step_km,
        0.99,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    max_step_km =
      max(
        step_km,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    p99_speed_kmh =
      quantile(
        speed_kmh,
        0.99,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    max_speed_kmh =
      max(
        speed_kmh,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    .groups = "drop"
  )


cat(
  "\n============================================================\n",
  "RAW TELEMETRY SUMMARY — NO LOCATION INFORMATION\n",
  "============================================================\n"
)

print(
  raw_summary,
  width = Inf
)


# =============================================================================
# 3. LARGEST STEPS
#
# No coordinates included.
# =============================================================================

largest_steps <- migr_raw_qc %>%

  filter(
    is.finite(step_km)
  ) %>%

  arrange(
    desc(step_km)
  ) %>%

  select(
    id,
    id_phase,
    previous_time,
    date_time,
    gap_hours,
    step_km,
    speed_kmh
  ) %>%

  slice_head(
    n = 30
  )


cat(
  "\n============================================================\n",
  "30 LARGEST RAW GPS STEPS — LOCATION REMOVED\n",
  "============================================================\n"
)

print(
  largest_steps,
  n = 30,
  width = Inf
)


# =============================================================================
# 4. RECALCULATE NUMBER OF FIXES IN EACH 7-DAY AKDE WINDOW
# =============================================================================

count_window_fixes <- function(
  akde_table,
  telemetry_table
) {

  akde_table %>%

    rowwise() %>%

    mutate(

      recalculated_n_fixes =
        sum(
          telemetry_table$id_phase ==
            id_phase &
          telemetry_table$date_time >=
            window_start &
          telemetry_table$date_time <=
            window_start +
            7 * 24 * 3600
        )
    ) %>%

    ungroup()
}


target_akde <- final %>%

  filter(
    id_phase %in% c(
      "A50_Phase_2",
      "F91_Phase_3",
      "A55_Phase_2"
    )
  )


target_with_counts <- count_window_fixes(
  target_akde,
  migr_raw_qc
)


# =============================================================================
# 5. FIX-COUNT SUMMARY
# =============================================================================

fix_count_summary <- target_with_counts %>%

  group_by(
    id_phase
  ) %>%

  summarise(

    minimum =
      min(
        recalculated_n_fixes
      ),

    median =
      median(
        recalculated_n_fixes
      ),

    maximum =
      max(
        recalculated_n_fixes
      ),

    .groups = "drop"
  )


cat(
  "\n============================================================\n",
  "RECALCULATED 7-DAY WINDOW FIX COUNTS\n",
  "============================================================\n"
)

print(
  fix_count_summary,
  width = Inf
)


# =============================================================================
# 6. FIX COUNTS FOR EXTREME AKDE WINDOWS
#
# Again: no coordinates.
# =============================================================================

extreme_windows_with_counts <- target_with_counts %>%

  mutate(

    relative_ci_width =
      (high - low) /
      est
  ) %>%

  filter(
    est > 500 |
    est < 0.01
  ) %>%

  select(
    id,
    id_phase,
    window_start,
    recalculated_n_fixes,
    low,
    est,
    high,
    relative_ci_width
  ) %>%

  arrange(
    id_phase,
    window_start
  )


cat(
  "\n============================================================\n",
  "EXTREME WINDOWS WITH RECALCULATED FIX COUNTS\n",
  "============================================================\n"
)

print(
  extreme_windows_with_counts,
  n = Inf,
  width = Inf
)


# =============================================================================
# 7. PRIVACY-SAFE RELATIVE TRACK PLOTS
#
# Coordinates are centered on the animal's first fix.
#
# (0,0) = first point.
#
# NO geographic location is recoverable from the axes.
# =============================================================================

plot_relative_track <- function(
  df,
  title_text
) {

  ggplot(
    df,
    aes(
      x = relative_x_km,
      y = relative_y_km
    )
  ) +

    geom_path(
      alpha = 0.6
    ) +

    geom_point(
      size = 1
    ) +

    coord_equal() +

    theme_bw(
      base_size = 12
    ) +

    labs(
      title = title_text,
      subtitle = "Coordinates centered to first fix; absolute location removed",
      x = "Relative east-west displacement (km)",
      y = "Relative north-south displacement (km)"
    )
}


# A50

A50_private <- migr_raw_qc %>%

  filter(
    id_phase == "A50_Phase_2",
    date_time >=
      as.POSIXct(
        "2008-06-03",
        tz = "UTC"
      ),
```

### IMpacts of extreme AKDE windows on training distriubtions
```{r}
# =============================================================================
# IMPACT OF EXTREME AKDE WINDOWS ON TRAINING DISTRIBUTION
# =============================================================================

library(dplyr)
library(tibble)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Define inspection flags only.
#
# These are NOT being removed from the dataset.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

impact_data <- train %>%

  mutate(

    high_AKDE_flag =
      akde_est > 500,

    tiny_AKDE_flag =
      akde_est < 0.01,

    either_extreme =
      high_AKDE_flag |
      tiny_AKDE_flag
  )


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. How many rows?
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

cat(
  "\n============================================================\n",
  "EXTREME AKDE PREVALENCE\n",
  "============================================================\n"
)


prevalence <- impact_data %>%

  summarise(

    total_AKDE_rows =
      sum(!is.na(akde_est)),

    high_rows =
      sum(high_AKDE_flag, na.rm = TRUE),

    tiny_rows =
      sum(tiny_AKDE_flag, na.rm = TRUE),

    either_rows =
      sum(either_extreme, na.rm = TRUE),

    percent_extreme =
      100 *
      either_rows /
      total_AKDE_rows
  )


print(
  prevalence,
  width = Inf
)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Full training distribution versus without flagged extremes
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

full_summary <- impact_data %>%

  filter(
    !is.na(akde_est)
  ) %>%

  summarise(

    version = "All corrected AKDE",

    n = n(),

    mean_low =
      mean(akde_low),

    sd_low =
      sd(akde_low),

    mean_est =
      mean(akde_est),

    sd_est =
      sd(akde_est),

    median_est =
      median(akde_est),

    mean_high =
      mean(akde_high),

    sd_high =
      sd(akde_high)
  )


without_extremes <- impact_data %>%

  filter(
    !is.na(akde_est),
    !either_extreme
  ) %>%

  summarise(

    version = "Without inspection extremes",

    n = n(),

    mean_low =
      mean(akde_low),

    sd_low =
      sd(akde_low),

    mean_est =
      mean(akde_est),

    sd_est =
      sd(akde_est),

    median_est =
      median(akde_est),

    mean_high =
      mean(akde_high),

    sd_high =
      sd(akde_high)
  )


comparison <- bind_rows(
  full_summary,
  without_extremes
)


cat(
  "\n============================================================\n",
  "SCALER-RELEVANT DISTRIBUTION COMPARISON\n",
  "============================================================\n"
)


print(
  comparison,
  width = Inf
)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Percent impact
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

impact_summary <- tibble(

  metric = c(
    "mean_low",
    "sd_low",
    "mean_est",
    "sd_est",
    "median_est",
    "mean_high",
    "sd_high"
  ),

  all_rows = c(
    full_summary$mean_low,
    full_summary$sd_low,
    full_summary$mean_est,
    full_summary$sd_est,
    full_summary$median_est,
    full_summary$mean_high,
    full_summary$sd_high
  ),

  without_flagged = c(
    without_extremes$mean_low,
    without_extremes$sd_low,
    without_extremes$mean_est,
    without_extremes$sd_est,
    without_extremes$median_est,
    without_extremes$mean_high,
    without_extremes$sd_high
  )
) %>%

  mutate(

    percent_change =
      100 *
      (
        without_flagged -
        all_rows
      ) /
      all_rows
  )


cat(
  "\n============================================================\n",
  "EFFECT OF FLAGGED WINDOWS ON TRAINING DISTRIBUTION\n",
  "============================================================\n"
)


print(
  impact_summary,
  n = Inf,
  width = Inf
)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Which animals contribute the flagged rows?
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

cat(
  "\n============================================================\n",
  "FLAGGED ROWS BY DEER\n",
  "============================================================\n"
)


impact_data %>%

  filter(
    either_extreme
  ) %>%

  count(
    dataset,
    id,
    id_phase,
    high_AKDE_flag,
    tiny_AKDE_flag,
    name = "n"
  ) %>%

  arrange(
    desc(n)
  ) %>%

  print(
    n = Inf,
    width = Inf
  )

```


### Fix Testing
```{r}
# =============================================================================
# PATCH CORRECTED AKDE INTO CWD-POSITIVE TEST DATA
#
# This does NOT:
#   - recalculate movement metrics
#   - recalculate AKDE
#   - change labels
#   - change row order
#   - change non-AKDE columns
#
# It ONLY replaces:
#   akde_low
#   akde_est
#   akde_high
#
# using:
#   Resident  -> resident_corrected
#   Migratory -> final
#
# Original AKDE missingness is preserved.
# =============================================================================

library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(tibble)


# =============================================================================
# 1. PATHS
# =============================================================================

BASE_DIR <-
  "<LOCAL_PATH>"


TEST_FILE <-
  file.path(
    BASE_DIR,
    "CWD_positive_testing_with_seasons2.csv"
  )


TEST_OUT <-
  file.path(
    BASE_DIR,
    "CWD_positive_testing_with_seasons2_AKDE_FIXED.csv"
  )


DIAGNOSTIC_OUT <-
  file.path(
    BASE_DIR,
    "CWD_positive_testing_MISSING_CORRECTED_AKDE.csv"
  )


# =============================================================================
# 2. CHECK REQUIRED OBJECTS / FILES
# =============================================================================

if (!file.exists(TEST_FILE)) {

  stop(
    paste0(
      "Original CWD-positive testing file does not exis<LOCAL_PATH>",
      TEST_FILE
    )
  )
}


if (!exists("resident_corrected")) {

  stop(
    "resident_corrected is not present in the R workspace."
  )
}


if (!exists("final")) {

  stop(
    paste0(
      "final is not present in the R workspace.\n",
      "This should contain the FINAL corrected migratory AKDE table."
    )
  )
}


# =============================================================================
# 3. TIMESTAMP NORMALIZER
#
# We create character join keys rather than relying on timezone-sensitive
# joins between POSIXct objects.
# =============================================================================

make_time_key <- function(x) {

  if (inherits(x, "POSIXt")) {

    parsed <-
      as.POSIXct(
        x,
        tz = "UTC"
      )

  } else {

    x_chr <-
      trimws(
        as.character(x)
      )

    # Remove trailing Z if present
    x_chr <-
      sub(
        "Z$",
        "",
        x_chr
      )

    parsed <-
      as.POSIXct(
        x_chr,
        tz = "UTC",
        tryFormats = c(
          "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%OS",
          "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%OS"
        )
      )
  }


  bad <-
    is.na(parsed) &
    !is.na(x)


  if (any(bad)) {

    stop(
      paste0(
        "Could not parse ",
        sum(bad),
        " timestamps."
      )
    )
  }


  format(
    parsed,
    format = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S",
    tz = "UTC"
  )
}


# =============================================================================
# 4. LOAD ORIGINAL CWD-POSITIVE TEST DATA
# =============================================================================

test_original <-
  read_csv(
    TEST_FILE,
    show_col_types = FALSE
  )


cat(
  "\n",
  paste(rep("=", 100), collapse = ""),
  "\n",
  "ORIGINAL CWD-POSITIVE TEST DATA\n",
  paste(rep("=", 100), collapse = ""),
  "\n",
  sep = ""
)


cat(
  "\nRows:",
  nrow(test_original),
  "\n"
)


cat(
  "Columns:",
  ncol(test_original),
  "\n"
)


cat(
  "Unique deer:",
  n_distinct(test_original$id),
  "\n"
)


# =============================================================================
# 5. REQUIRED COLUMN CHECKS
# =============================================================================

required_test_columns <-
  c(
    "id",
    "dataset",
    "date_time",
    "akde_low",
    "akde_est",
    "akde_high"
  )


missing_test_columns <-
  setdiff(
    required_test_columns,
    names(test_original)
  )


if (length(missing_test_columns) > 0) {

  stop(
    paste(
      "Testing data missing required columns:",
      paste(
        missing_test_columns,
        collapse = ", "
      )
    )
  )
}


# Normalize dataset label

dataset_normalized <-
  tolower(
    trimws(
      as.character(
        test_original$dataset
      )
    )
  )


cat(
  "\nDataset value<LOCAL_PATH>"
)


print(
  table(
    dataset_normalized,
    useNA = "ifany"
  )
)


# If migratory rows exist, id_phase MUST already exist.
# We do NOT reconstruct it silently.

if (
  any(
    dataset_normalized == "migratory",
    na.rm = TRUE
  ) &&
  !"id_phase" %in% names(test_original)
) {

  stop(
    paste0(
      "Migratory rows exist, but id_phase is absent.\n",
      "Stop here rather than reconstructing phase labels."
    )
  )
}


# =============================================================================
# 6. BUILD CORRECTED RESIDENT LOOKUP
# =============================================================================

resident_lookup <-
  resident_corrected %>%

  transmute(

    id =
      as.character(id),

    .join_time =
      make_time_key(
        window_start
      ),

    resident_low =
      as.numeric(low),

    resident_est =
      as.numeric(est),

    resident_high =
      as.numeric(high)
  )


resident_duplicates <-
  resident_lookup %>%

  count(
    id,
    .join_time
  ) %>%

  filter(
    n > 1
  )


if (nrow(resident_duplicates) > 0) {

  stop(
    "Duplicate corrected resident AKDE join keys found."
  )
}


# =============================================================================
# 7. BUILD CORRECTED MIGRATORY LOOKUP
# =============================================================================

migratory_lookup <-
  final %>%

  transmute(

    id_phase =
      as.character(id_phase),

    .join_time =
      make_time_key(
        window_start
      ),

    migratory_low =
      as.numeric(low),

    migratory_est =
      as.numeric(est),

    migratory_high =
      as.numeric(high)
  )


migratory_duplicates <-
  migratory_lookup %>%

  count(
    id_phase,
    .join_time
  ) %>%

  filter(
    n > 1
  )


if (nrow(migratory_duplicates) > 0) {

  stop(
    "Duplicate corrected migratory AKDE join keys found."
  )
}


# =============================================================================
# 8. PREPARE ORIGINAL TEST DATA
# =============================================================================

test_work <-
  test_original %>%

  mutate(

    .row_id =
      row_number(),

    id =
      as.character(id),

    .dataset_normalized =
      tolower(
        trimws(
          as.character(dataset)
        )
      ),

    .join_time =
      make_time_key(
        date_time
      ),

    # Preserve ORIGINAL AKDE missingness
    .original_low_present =
      !is.na(akde_low),

    .original_est_present =
      !is.na(akde_est),

    .original_high_present =
      !is.na(akde_high)
  )


if ("id_phase" %in% names(test_work)) {

  test_work <-
    test_work %>%

    mutate(
      id_phase =
        as.character(id_phase)
    )
}


# =============================================================================
# 9. JOIN BOTH CORRECTED SOURCE TABLES
# =============================================================================

test_joined <-
  test_work %>%

  left_join(
    resident_lookup,
    by = c(
      "id",
      ".join_time"
    )
  ) %>%

  left_join(
    migratory_lookup,
    by = c(
      "id_phase",
      ".join_time"
    )
  )


# The joins must NEVER change row count

if (
  nrow(test_joined) !=
  nrow(test_original)
) {

  stop(
    paste0(
      "Join changed row count.\n",
      "Original: ",
      nrow(test_original),
      "\nAfter join: ",
      nrow(test_joined)
    )
  )
}


# =============================================================================
# 10. CHOOSE CORRECTED SOURCE BASED ON ORIGINAL DATASET LABEL
# =============================================================================

test_joined <-
  test_joined %>%

  mutate(

    corrected_low =
      case_when(

        .dataset_normalized == "resident" ~
          resident_low,

        .dataset_normalized == "migratory" ~
          migratory_low,

        TRUE ~
          NA_real_
      ),


    corrected_est =
      case_when(

        .dataset_normalized == "resident" ~
          resident_est,

        .dataset_normalized == "migratory" ~
          migratory_est,

        TRUE ~
          NA_real_
      ),


    corrected_high =
      case_when(

        .dataset_normalized == "resident" ~
          resident_high,

        .dataset_normalized == "migratory" ~
          migratory_high,

        TRUE ~
          NA_real_
      ),


    .original_any_akde =
      .original_low_present |
      .original_est_present |
      .original_high_present
  )


# =============================================================================
# 11. CHECK EVERY EXISTING AKDE ROW HAS A CORRECTED SOURCE MATCH
# =============================================================================

missing_corrected <-
  test_joined %>%

  filter(
    .original_any_akde,
    (
      is.na(corrected_low) |
      is.na(corrected_est) |
      is.na(corrected_high)
    )
  )


cat(
  "\n",
  paste(rep("=", 100), collapse = ""),
  "\n",
  "CORRECTED AKDE MATCH CHECK\n",
  paste(rep("=", 100), collapse = ""),
  "\n",
  sep = ""
)


cat(
  "\nRows in original testing data:",
  nrow(test_original),
  "\n"
)


cat(
  "Rows that originally had AKDE:",
  sum(
    test_joined$.original_any_akde
  ),
  "\n"
)


cat(
  "Rows missing corrected AKDE matches:",
  nrow(missing_corrected),
  "\n"
)


if (nrow(missing_corrected) > 0) {

  write_csv(
    missing_corrected,
    DIAGNOSTIC_OUT
  )

  stop(
    paste0(
      "Some testing rows with existing AKDE do not have corrected matches.\n",
      "Diagnostic saved t<LOCAL_PATH>",
      DIAGNOSTIC_OUT
    )
  )
}


# =============================================================================
# 12. REPLACE ONLY THE THREE AKDE COLUMNS
#
# IMPORTANT:
# Missingness is preserved PER COLUMN.
# =============================================================================

test_fixed <-
  test_joined %>%

  mutate(

    akde_low =
      if_else(
        .original_low_present,
        corrected_low,
        NA_real_
      ),

    akde_est =
      if_else(
        .original_est_present,
        corrected_est,
        NA_real_
      ),

    akde_high =
      if_else(
        .original_high_present,
        corrected_high,
        NA_real_
      )
  ) %>%

  arrange(
    .row_id
  )


# =============================================================================
# 13. REMOVE ALL TEMPORARY JOIN COLUMNS
# =============================================================================

helper_columns <-
  c(
    ".row_id",
    ".dataset_normalized",
    ".join_time",
    ".original_low_present",
    ".original_est_present",
    ".original_high_present",
    ".original_any_akde",
    "resident_low",
    "resident_est",
    "resident_high",
    "migratory_low",
    "migratory_est",
    "migratory_high",
    "corrected_low",
    "corrected_est",
    "corrected_high"
  )


test_fixed <-
  test_fixed %>%

  select(
    -any_of(
      helper_columns
    )
  )


# Restore exact original column ordering

test_fixed <-
  test_fixed[
    names(test_original)
  ]


# =============================================================================
# 14. PROVE THAT NO NON-AKDE COLUMN CHANGED
# =============================================================================

non_akde_columns <-
  setdiff(
    names(test_original),
    c(
      "akde_low",
      "akde_est",
      "akde_high"
    )
  )


if (
  !identical(
    test_original[
      non_akde_columns
    ],
    test_fixed[
      non_akde_columns
    ]
  )
) {

  stop(
    paste0(
      "A non-AKDE column changed unexpectedly.\n",
      "Do NOT save this file."
    )
  )
}


cat(
  "\nPASS: every non-AKDE column is unchanged.\n"
)


# =============================================================================
# 15. FINAL AKDE VALIDATION
# =============================================================================

bad_numeric <-
  test_fixed %>%

  filter(
    !is.na(akde_est) &
    (
      !is.finite(akde_low) |
      !is.finite(akde_est) |
      !is.finite(akde_high)
    )
  )


bad_positive <-
  test_fixed %>%

  filter(
    !is.na(akde_est) &
    (
      akde_low <= 0 |
      akde_est <= 0 |
      akde_high <= 0
    )
  )


bad_ci <-
  test_fixed %>%

  filter(
    !is.na(akde_est) &
    (
      akde_low > akde_est |
      akde_est > akde_high
    )
  )


cat(
  "\n",
  paste(rep("=", 100), collapse = ""),
  "\n",
  "FINAL CORRECTED TEST AKDE VALIDATION\n",
  paste(rep("=", 100), collapse = ""),
  "\n",
  sep = ""
)


cat(
  "\nNon-finite AKDE rows:",
  nrow(bad_numeric),
  "\n"
)


cat(
  "Non-positive AKDE rows:",
  nrow(bad_positive),
  "\n"
)


cat(
  "Invalid CI-order rows:",
  nrow(bad_ci),
  "\n"
)


if (
  nrow(bad_numeric) > 0 |
  nrow(bad_positive) > 0 |
  nrow(bad_ci) > 0
) {

  stop(
    "Corrected testing data failed AKDE validation."
  )
}


# =============================================================================
# 16. SAVE CORRECTED TEST FILE
# =============================================================================

write_csv(
  test_fixed,
  TEST_OUT,
  na = ""
)


# =============================================================================
# 17. FINAL REPORT
# =============================================================================

cat(
  "\n",
  paste(rep("=", 100), collapse = ""),
  "\n",
  "SUCCESS: CORRECTED CWD-POSITIVE TEST FILE CREATED\n",
  paste(rep("=", 100), collapse = ""),
  "\n",
  sep = ""
)


cat(
  "\nRows:",
  nrow(test_fixed),
  "\n"
)


cat(
  "Unique deer:",
  n_distinct(test_fixed$id),
  "\n"
)


cat(
  "Rows with corrected AKDE:",
  sum(!is.na(test_fixed$akde_est)),
  "\n"
)


cat(
  "\nSaved t<LOCAL_PATH>",
  TEST_OUT,
  "\n",
  sep = ""
)

```


### Final trim
```{r}

# =============================================================================
# TRIM CORRECTED TRAINING AND TESTING DATASETS
#
# QC rule:
#   Remove rows where akde_est > 150 km^2
#
# Important:
#   - Keeps rows with missing AKDE unchanged
#   - Does NOT modify any values
#   - Does NOT recalculate movement metrics
#   - Does NOT remove tiny AKDE estimates
#   - Preserves every original column
#
# Outputs:
#   CWD_negative_training_with_seasons2_AKDE_FIXED_TRIMMED_150.csv
#   CWD_positive_testing_with_seasons2_AKDE_FIXED_TRIMMED_150.csv
# =============================================================================


library(
  dplyr
)

library(
  readr
)


# =============================================================================
# 1. SETTINGS
# =============================================================================

BASE_DIR <-
  "<LOCAL_PATH>"

  file.path(

  )


TEST_FILE <-
  file.path(

  )


TRAIN_OUT <-
  file.path(

    "CWD_negative_training_with_seasons2_AKDE_FIXED_TRIMMED_150.csv"
  )


TEST_OUT <-
  file.path(
    BASE_DIR,
    "CWD_positive_testing_with_seasons2_AKDE_FIXED_TRIMMED_150.csv"
  )


AKDE_MAX_KM2 <- 150


# =============================================================================
# 2. CHECK THAT BOTH INPUT FILES EXIST
# =============================================================================

if (!file.exists(TRAIN_FILE)) {

# =============================================================================

train_original <-

)

    train_original
  ),
  "\n"
)


cat(

  nrow(
    test_original
  ),
  "\n"

  ),

# =============================================================================
# 4. REQUIRED COLUMN CHECK
# =============================================================================

required_akde_columns <-
  c(
    "akde_low",

  )


missing_train_columns <-
  setdiff(
    required_akde_columns,

if (

  ) > 0
) {

  stop(

        missing_train_columns,

}


if (
  length(

  ) > 0
) {

      "Testing data are missing:",
      paste(
        missing_test_columns,
        collapse = ", "
      )
    )

}


# =============================================================================
# 5. BASIC AKDE VALIDATION BEFORE FILTERING
# =============================================================================

validate_akde <- function(
  data,
  dataset_name
) {

  bad_numeric <-
    data %>%

    filter(
      !is.na(
        akde_est
      ) &
      (
        !is.finite(
          akde_low
        ) |
        !is.finite(
          akde_est
        ) |
        !is.finite(
          akde_high
        )
      )
    )


  bad_positive <-
    data %>%

    filter(
      !is.na(
        akde_est
      ) &
      (
        akde_low <= 0 |
        akde_est <= 0 |
        akde_high <= 0
      )
    )


  bad_ci <-
    data %>%

    filter(
      !is.na(
        akde_est
      ) &
      (
        akde_low > akde_est |
        akde_est > akde_high
      )
    )


  cat(
    "\n",
    dataset_name,
    "\n",
    sep = ""
  )


  cat(
    "Non-finite AKDE rows:",
    nrow(
      bad_numeric
    ),
    "\n"
  )


  cat(
    "Non-positive AKDE rows:",
    nrow(
      bad_positive
    ),
    "\n"
  )


  cat(
    "Invalid CI ordering rows:",
    nrow(
      bad_ci
    ),
    "\n"
  )


  if (
    nrow(
      bad_numeric
    ) > 0 |
    nrow(
      bad_positive
    ) > 0 |
    nrow(
      bad_ci
    ) > 0
  ) {

    stop(
      paste0(
        dataset_name,
        " failed AKDE validation."
      )
    )
  }
}


cat(
  "\n",
  paste(
    rep(

      100
    ),
    collapse = ""
  ),
  "\n",
  "PRE-TRIM AKDE VALIDATION\n",
  paste(
    rep(
      "=",
      100
    ),
    collapse = ""
  ),
  "\n",
  sep = ""
)


validate_akde(
  train_original,
  "CWD-negative training"
)


validate_akde(
  test_original,
  "CWD-positive testing"
)


# =============================================================================
# 6. IDENTIFY ROWS >150 KM^2
# =============================================================================

train_removed <-
  train_original %>%

  filter(
    !is.na(
      akde_est
    ),
    akde_est > AKDE_MAX_KM2
  )


test_removed <-
  test_original %>%

  filter(
    !is.na(
      akde_est
    ),
    akde_est > AKDE_MAX_KM2
  )


# =============================================================================
# 7. SUMMARIZE REMOVED ROWS
# =============================================================================

summarize_removed <- function(
  removed_data,
  dataset_name
) {

  cat(
    "\n",
    paste(
      rep(
        "=",
        100
      ),
      collapse = ""
    ),
    "\n",
    dataset_name,
    " — ROWS ABOVE 150 KM^2\n",
    paste(
      rep(
        "=",
        100
      ),
      collapse = ""
    ),
    "\n",
    sep = ""
  )


  cat(
    "\nRows:",
    nrow(
      removed_data
    ),
    "\n"
  )


  if (
    nrow(
      removed_data
    ) > 0
  ) {

    cat(
      "Minimum removed akde_est:",
      min(
        removed_data$akde_est,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),
      "\n"
    )


    cat(
      "Median removed akde_est:",
      median(
        removed_data$akde_est,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),
      "\n"
    )


    cat(
      "Maximum removed akde_est:",
      max(
        removed_data$akde_est,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),
      "\n"
    )


    if (
      "id" %in%
      names(
        removed_data
      )
    ) {

      group_columns <-
        intersect(
          c(
            "dataset",
            "id",
            "id_phase"
          ),
          names(
            removed_data
          )
        )


      removed_summary <-
        removed_data %>%

        group_by(
          across(
            all_of(
              group_columns
            )
          )
        ) %>%

        summarise(

          n_removed =
            n(),

          minimum =
            min(
              akde_est,
              na.rm = TRUE
            ),

          median =
            median(
              akde_est,
              na.rm = TRUE
            ),

          maximum =
            max(
              akde_est,
              na.rm = TRUE
            ),

          .groups = "drop"
        ) %>%

        arrange(
          desc(
            n_removed
          )
        )


      print(
        removed_summary,
        n = Inf,
        width = Inf
      )
    }
  }
}


summarize_removed(
  train_removed,
  "CWD-NEGATIVE TRAINING"
)


summarize_removed(
  test_removed,
  "CWD-POSITIVE TESTING"
)


# =============================================================================
# 8. TRIM ONLY AKDE_EST >150
#
# Missing AKDE values are retained.
# =============================================================================

train_trimmed <-
  train_original %>%

  filter(
    is.na(
      akde_est
    ) |
    akde_est <= AKDE_MAX_KM2
  )


test_trimmed <-
  test_original %>%

  filter(
    is.na(
      akde_est
    ) |
    akde_est <= AKDE_MAX_KM2
  )


# =============================================================================
# 9. HARD VALIDATION OF FILTERING
# =============================================================================

if (
  any(
    train_trimmed$akde_est >
      AKDE_MAX_KM2,
    na.rm = TRUE
  )
) {

  stop(
    "Training data still contain akde_est > 150."
  )
}


if (
  any(
    test_trimmed$akde_est >
      AKDE_MAX_KM2,
    na.rm = TRUE
  )
) {

  stop(
    "Testing data still contain akde_est > 150."
  )
}


# Number removed must equal number flagged

if (
  nrow(
    train_original
  ) -
  nrow(
    train_trimmed
  ) !=
  nrow(
    train_removed
  )
) {

  stop(
    "Training row-count validation failed."
  )
}


if (
  nrow(
    test_original
  ) -
  nrow(
    test_trimmed
  ) !=
  nrow(
    test_removed
  )
) {

  stop(
    "Testing row-count validation failed."
  )
}


# Column names and order must be unchanged

if (
  !identical(
    names(
      train_original
    ),
    names(
      train_trimmed
    )
  )
) {

  stop(
    "Training columns changed unexpectedly."
  )
}


if (
  !identical(
    names(
      test_original
    ),
    names(
      test_trimmed
    )
  )
) {
```
